rows.note: Use this for the power or authority to influence a decision or have the final say; it is the all-purpose choice for that slice.

example.english: I also have the final say in this matter.
example.jyutping: ni1 daan1 je5 ngo5 dou1 jau5 waa6 si6 kyun4

rows.note: Use this when the focus is on having the right or opportunity to speak in a discussion or decision.

example.english: At this meeting, everyone has the right to speak and have a say.
example.traditional: 今次開會，人人都有發言權。
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 hoi1 wui6 jan4 jan4 dou1 jau5 faat3 jin4 kyun4

rows.note: Use 講 as the all-purpose spoken verb for pronouncing something, speaking or expressing an opinion, and in 我敢講 for expressing strong belief.

example.english: I dare say they'll definitely win tomorrow.
example.traditional: 我敢講佢聽日一定會贏。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gam2 gong2 keoi5 ting1 jat6 jat1 ding6 wui5 jeng4

rows.note: Use 話 when reporting what someone says or introducing a rumour or commonly repeated statement.

example.english: People say the shop will close next month.
example.traditional: 聽人話間舖下個月結業。
example.jyutping: ting1 jan4 waa6 gaan1 pou3 haa6 go3 jyut6 git3 jip6

rows.note: Use 寫住 when a sign, notice, or other written text indicates information.

example.english: The sign seems to say that parking is not allowed here.
example.jyutping: go3 paai4 se2 zyu6 m4 zeon2 paak3 ce1

rows.note: Use 假設 to introduce an assumption or hypothetical case, rather than to report an actual utterance.

example.english: Let's say you don't have to work tomorrow; shall we go hiking?
example.traditional: 假設你聽日唔使返工，我哋去行山啦。
example.jyutping: gaa2 cit3 nei5 ting1 jat6 m4 sai2 faan1 gung1 ngo5 dei6 heoi3 haang4 saan1 laa1
